data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "The system should merge conclusions only when forced by resource exhaustion, using a similarity metric that prioritizes merging the most similar pair first, and should otherwise keep all conclusions distinct to avoid premature unification.", "mechanism": "A resource monitor triggers merging when memory or inference time exceeds a threshold. The system computes a similarity score based on shared predicates, constants, and derivation overlap, then merges the highest-scoring pair into a single claim with a disjunctive scope note. The threshold for similarity is dynamically lowered as resources become scarcer.", "scope": {"covers": ["resource-bounded reasoning systems"], "excludes": ["systems with unlimited memory and time"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Merging two similar but distinct claims under resource pressure leads to a contradiction that would not have arisen if they were kept separate, and the system had sufficient resources to maintain both.", "eval": "program:merge_induced_contradiction"}, {"case": "The system refuses to merge any claims despite resource exhaustion, causing a crash or infinite loop that could have been avoided by merging.", "eval": "program:resource_exhaustion_no_merge"}], "prose_notes": "This is a risk-management approach that treats merging as a necessary evil under scarcity, explicitly trading off accuracy for survival. It risks both over-merging (when similarity metric is too permissive) and under-merging (when threshold is too strict)."}
